title: Open a keypad home safe: key the code, turn the knob within the 5 s the green light gives, swing the door open
instruction: Open the safe, leave its door open and take your hands away. The code is 1 7 5 0 0, then the # key.
context: Small keypad safes like SentrySafe's X055 are sold for homes and offices, and many hotel rooms have one. Opening one has a catch anyone who has used one knows. The maker's manual: 'Enter your factory code or user code followed by #. The green LED light will go and remain on for 5 seconds. Within 5 seconds, turn the knob clockwise and pull open the door.' Miss the window and the knob stays locked, so the code has to be keyed again; a wrong key costs a minute's wait. So six small keys on a 16 mm pitch are each pressed through their click without touching a neighbour, and the knob is gripped and turned a quarter turn as soon as the light comes on, which draws the bolts. The door is then pulled open by the knob on its left hinge, toward the robot. One hand alone can do all of it if it gets from the # key to the knob inside the 5 seconds. SentrySafe is a trademark of Master Lock Company LLC, named for identification only.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bare wooden table top. (1) A SentrySafe X055 digital security safe (powder-coated steel; 35.1 wide, 22.1 high, 24.6 deep, 6.44 kg: the maker's listing) stands loose on the table, door facing the robot, its front face at x 38, centred at y 0. Steel on wood friction 0.4. Door (estimates from the listed size; the maker publishes no drawings): 33 x 19 cm, 1.8 cm thick, 2.3 kg, set in the front face with 1.5 mm clearance, hinged on its left edge (y +16.5) on a vertical axis, hinge friction 0.02 N m, 100 degree stop; the safe's own body is 4.1 kg. Keypad on the door's right half: 12 round keys (1 2 3 / 4 5 6 / 7 8 9 / * 0 #), 1.0 across, in three columns 1.6 apart (y -3.4, -5.0, -6.6) and four rows 1.4 apart (z 17.1, 15.7, 14.3, 12.9), each 2 mm proud of the door, 1 mm of travel on a spring: 1.0 N at rest, a 2.4 N click at 0.7 mm. A green and a yellow light, 0.7 cm across, above the keys at (38, -4.2, 19.0) and (38, -5.8, 19.0). Knob: round, 4.5 across and 2.2 long, standing out of the door at (38, -11, 10.5), turning 90 degrees clockwise seen from the robot, held at 0 by the lock except while the green light is on, with 0.1 N m of friction and a red marker line along its top at 0. It stays where it is turned (the manual locks the safe by turning it back); no return spring. Once the knob has passed 80 degrees the bolts are drawn and the door swings free. Lock: the code 1-7-5-0-0 then #; the green light stays on 5.0 s; any other code before # gives the yellow light, and the keys are ignored for 60 s. Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Reset: door shut, knob at 0 so the bolts are out, lights off.
scoring: Read from the key, knob and door joints and the lock's state; in a real trial from a video showing the lights, the knob's marker line and the door, a protractor on the hinge. 0.25: the code is accepted (green light). 0.5: the knob turned past 80 degrees while the green light was on. 0.75: the door open 20 degrees or more. 1.0: the door open 70 degrees or more, every fingertip of both grippers 3 cm clear of the safe, and all still for 1 s. Score 0 if the safe moves more than 2 cm or tips more than 5 degrees. The run ends with success once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz), about 2.5 times the 24 s demo
reset_notes: Nothing is random: the door shut, the knob at 0, the lock idle.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz, GPU. Safe at SentrySafe's listed outer size and mass; door size and mass, key size, pitch and travel, click force, knob size, steel-on-wood, knob and hinge friction are estimates (no drawings). The lock's electronics are code: a key counts when its own travel passes the 0.7 mm click, 1-7-5-0-0-# opens a 5.0 s window, the knob is held at 0 outside it, bolts are drawn past 80 degrees of knob, a wrong code gives the yellow light and 60 s of ignored keys.
scores: Demo: 1.0 (both hands, 487 steps, 24 s). Right hand alone: 1.0 (440 steps). Wrong code 0; code then knob after the light 0.25; knob turned before the code 0; door pulled shut 0 (safe dragged 46 mm); keys only touched 0; nothing 0. Dream-1 run: 0.0.
